claims.text: The LLAMA3 model achieved an accuracy of 0.84 for binary classification of coded interview segments.
The LLAMA3 model achieved an accuracy of 0.67 for independent classification using a sliding window approach.
LLM performance in coding interview data demonstrated large variability across different qualitative codes.
Around 80% of LLM-generated summaries were rated as 'adequate' or 'good' by two independent researchers.

evidence.description: the LLM achieved substantial agreement with the researchers for the binary classification (accuracy: 0.84)
The performance had large variability across codes.
around 80% of the summaries being rated independently by two researchers as 'adequate' or 'good.'

methodologies.name: LLM-based Deductive Coding and Summarization
methodologies.description: Evaluation of a server-installed LLAMA3 model performing binary classification, sliding window classification, and summarization on psychosocial autopsy interview data using Cohen's Kappa and the Constant Comparative Method.
datasets: 38 semi-structured interviews with individuals bereaved by suicide
conditions: independent classification using a sliding window approach

limitations.text: Qualitative research is often prone to bias and is time- and cost-intensive.
Model performance had large variability across different codes.
LLM summaries exhibited issues with unsolicited elaboration and hallucination.

future_work.text: Replicate the findings across different qualitative contexts.
Evaluate language models with a larger context size.
